A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PositionIC and retain the same data-synthesis pipeline and principal benchmarks. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. The supplied v1 ends with references; v4 includes supplementary Sections 6–10, which were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original DreamBench and PositionIC-Bench evaluations, qualitative generation results, and data-filter and attention-mask ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds human evaluations, filter–human agreement results, occlusion experiments, and supplementary ablations.

M1.justification: v1 uses a binary regional Attention Horizon mask. v4 introduces Visibility-Aware Attention with NeRF-inspired Volumetric Weight Regulation, using semantic densities and depth ordering to weight attention and handle overlapping subjects (Sections 3.2 and 8.1). This changes the attention procedure; the BMPDS pipeline and FLUX/LoRA backbone remain.

E1.justification: Subject200K, PIC-400K/PIC-98K, DreamBench, and PositionIC-Bench remain, including the latter's 252 single-subject and 296 multi-subject samples. v4 adds explicit depth-ordered overlap scenarios in Figure 9 and additional demonstrations, including space scenes in Figure 12. This modestly extends tested scenarios without introducing a new principal benchmark.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the corresponding qualitative comparisons. RegionalFlux is renamed RPF. The new human evaluation reuses UNO, OmniGen, DreamO, and OminiControl, already evaluated against PositionIC in v1; newly cited methods such as GroundingBooth and LaRender are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds a human-evaluation protocol using 500 randomly selected images, six evaluators, and five criteria scored from 0 to 5, plus filter agreement measured across data-quality intervals. It also specifies disabling VWR by setting overlap-region attention to 1 and adds CLIP-T to the data-filter comparison. Existing benchmark sizes, training budgets, and subject-cropping evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds controlled overlap/non-overlap VWR case studies, qualitative removal of filtering and VAA separately and together, and human validation of the filter. The original attention-mask ablation is retained under VAA terminology in the appendix. The data-filter analysis also changes from checkpoint-wise CLIP-I/DINO curves to three-metric bar summaries, removing training-trajectory evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4's human-rating averages and filter-agreement score are point estimates; they do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The reported single-subject DINO score changes from 0.828 to 0.823 in Tables 1 and 4; Tables 2 and 3 retain their values. v4 adds human-rating results, average filter–human agreement of 0.89, and qualitative occlusion and joint-ablation findings. Figure 7 replaces checkpoint results with bar summaries and adds CLIP-T results. These are revised or additional results, not evidence of a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's binary mask formulation, v4 introduces continuous and discretized volume-rendering expressions, a recursive volumetric mask definition, and a geometric semantic-density schedule (Equations 2–4 and 8). These substantively expand the mathematical formulation underlying attention. No theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v4 elevates visibility-aware, occlusion-controllable generation through VWR to a central contribution and explicitly claims BMPDS is the first automatic pipeline for position-annotated multi-subject datasets. The abstract and introduction broaden the spatial-control claim to occlusion and perspective relationships. The general claims of leading identity consistency and spatial precision were already present in v1.

C2.justification: v1 primarily explains attention restriction as concentrating feature transfer and accelerating convergence. v4 adds a visibility and semantic-density account of occlusion, interpreting failures without VWR as incorrect depth ordering or missing objects caused by concept confusion. Human agreement newly supports the interpretation that the filter matches human judgments. Neither version develops a substantive limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the GPT-4o filtering prompt, feature-selection requirements, 0–5 scoring rubric, response format, and worked examples. It also documents dataset composition, benchmark bounding-box adjustments, and the semantic-density schedule with training parameter lambda set to 5. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the original hardware and training settings remain, and neither PDF provides an actual code/data release.

R1.justification: v4 positions the revised mechanism through volume rendering and NeRF, adds occlusion/layout references such as LaRender, LayoutCoT, and CreatiDesign, and expands personalization references with FastComposer and GroundingBooth. It also strengthens BMPDS's novelty positioning to a first-of-its-kind claim. References including HiDream-I1, Playground v2, and SSR-Encoder are removed, although SSR-Encoder remains an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around an explicit task definition, coupled data/attention bottlenecks, and visibility-aware control. v4 introduces a numbered section hierarchy and a structured supplement. Existing cropping-metric discussion and the attention-mask ablation move into that supplement, while substantial parts of the original experiments and conclusion remain.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redrawn to explain visibility-aware attention and volumetric weighting. The teaser is rearranged, the filter learning curves become bar charts, and new human-study, occlusion, dataset, prompt, and ablation displays are added. The cropping graphic and Table 4 move to the supplement; several existing qualitative comparisons are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility through the detailed filtering prompt and implementation disclosures, and strengthens support through human evaluation and targeted occlusion controls. The gains are limited by VWR's reliance on two qualitative case studies and the removal of checkpoint-wise filter results; most principal benchmark results remain unchanged. The clearest net improvement is better documentation and validation, rather than a demonstrated substantial improvement in the central empirical conclusions.
